paper_metadata.title: Effect of Ti/Ta ratio on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Hf20Mo15Nb25Ta20-xTi20+x refractory high-entropy alloys

evidence.quote: The limited deformation capacity at room temperature remains a significant challenge in refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs).

In a previous study [26] , the authors prepared fine-grained HfMoNbTaTi alloys via the MA and SPS process, which demonstrated an increase in room-temperature compressive yield strength by 35.73 % and plastic strain by 120.33 % in comparison to the as-cast alloys.

The optimum MA process parameters have been obtained in previous work [27] : rotational speed: 400 rpm, ball-to-power weight ratio: 10:1, and milling time: 50 h.
The heating rate, sintering pressure, and holding time were 50 ℃ /min, 50 MPa, and 15 min, respectively. The as-sintered alloys were cooled to room temperature within the furnace.
